answers.how: The car spans about 517 pixels in the side view; the tire diameter is about 84 pixels. Thus 517 × 0.764 / 84 ≈ 4.70 m.
The rear pillar markings are about 39 pixels tall. Correcting the tire scale to the approximately 23.44 m rear-wall depth gives about 0.73 m.
The rear pillar's front face is approximately 51 pixels wide. Applying the depth-corrected tire scale gives about 0.96 m.
A local fit to the front tire's horizontal positions gives approximately 682 pixels/s at 0.5 s. Multiplying by 0.764/84 converts this to 6.2 m/s.
The local curvature of the tire-position trajectory near 0.5 s is approximately 1245 pixels/s², giving 11.3 m/s² using the tire scale.
The tire moves at approximately 1055 pixels/s near 1 s. Using 0.764/84 meters per pixel gives 9.6 m/s.
A local polynomial fit to tire positions around 1 s gives approximately 242 pixels/s², equivalent to 2.2 m/s².
The B1 lettering spans approximately 81 pixels. Its scale is (0.764/84) × (23.44/11.38) meters per pixel, giving 1.52 m.
The lettering is approximately 75 pixels tall. Applying the tire scale and the 23.44/11.38 depth correction gives 1.41 m.
Using the floor's vanishing point and the known rear-wall depth, successive corresponding pillar faces have an estimated depth spacing of about 6.3 m.
